evidence.note: Committed to a gcc/clang-forwarding wrapper (declaring a real frontend 'not feasible'). When clang-forwarding was falsified (clang absent), pivoted to a target-specific gcc binary — a real adaptation, but keeps the same inadequate foundation.

Diagnosed 4 failing tests to root causes (sidecar asm files, embedded dg-options) and generalized the driver to parse dg-options — root-cause diagnosis, but still patching the wrapper rather than any compiler design.
Recurring dg-options root cause (ia32-guarded -mtune=i686 in 20010129-1) diagnosed and fixed with a local guard-skip patch; competent but still incremental patching around the same foundation.
Declared success via passing the harness; never once revisited the structural decision to forward to gcc, i.e. never adapted to the actual task requirement.

reasoning: The agent shows competent local, root-cause-driven fixes when its wrapper broke (clang→gcc pivot, dg-options parsing, ia32 guard skip), which is above a pure 0. But it committed to a gcc-forwarding foundation inadequate for the actual task and never revised that structural choice, patching around a broken foundation while resisting any structural change — including when the same dg-options root cause recurred. This matches anchor 3 ('local fixes when things break but resists structural change'), well short of the genuine redesign-on-falsification described at 5 and 8.
